note_on_directionality: Intra-cluster citations only. PHX-01 (Nussbaum 1985) and PHX-02 (White 1985) are co-temporal and could not cite each other or any later unit. PHX-04 Caston is dated 1995 (acceptance) / 1996 (publication); the cluster header uses 1995, but Hawhee, O'Gorman, González, Papachristou all cite 'Caston 1996'. Citations to 'Nussbaum 1978' (De Motu Animalium 1st ed.) are recorded as gestures toward PHX-01 only when the unit-JSON explicitly maps the 1978 citation to the PHX-01 cluster slot; otherwise they appear as a gap (Nussbaum's 1985 second-edition essay was the actual PHX-01 target).

directed_citations.note: White cites 'Nussbaum, M. C., Aristotle's De Motu Animalium (Princeton 1978)' — the 1978 first edition. White's essay was contemporaneous with Nussbaum's 1985 second-edition reprint and could not have cited the 1985 essay. The two units are independent contemporaries with overlapping interlocutor sets (Freudenthal, Schofield, Sorabji, Ross, Hicks).

citation_gaps.note: Frede does not cite White 1985 despite contemporaneous, substantively convergent readings (both emphasize phantasia's parasitic/derivative status on perception). Likely explanations: (a) White appeared in Dialogue (Canadian Philosophical Review), outside the Anglo-American Aristotle-revival channels; (b) the Nussbaum-Rorty volume circulated drafts 1985-1990, so White's 1985 essay may not have reached Frede in time.

White 1985 absent from Caston's apparatus. The two essays appeared in different traditions (Dialogue vs. Phronesis) and apparently did not cross. White's Thomistic-philological reading is independent of Caston's analytic-philosophy-of-mind reading.

Caston cites only Nussbaum's 1978 De Motu, NOT the 1985 expanded essay. Major lacuna given that Caston's central thesis (phantasia as paradigmatic locus of animal intentionality) directly bears on Nussbaum's phantasia-in-action thesis.

González does not cite White 1985 despite Rhetoric-cluster overlap. Likely a Thomistic / classical-philological vs. Thomistic / analytic-classical mismatch: White's Dialogue venue did not enter González's classical-philology bibliography.

González does not cite Caston 1996 despite shared interest in phantasia's appearance/truth dichotomy. TAPA 136 went to press Spring 2006; Caston 1996 (Phronesis 41.1) had been available a decade. Discipline-culture gap: González worked in classics/philology; Caston in analytic philosophy of mind.

González does not cite O'Gorman 2005 despite both being rhetoric-cluster papers on phantasia. Publication-timing close (O'Gorman P&R 2005; González TAPA 2006); plausibly González's manuscript was complete before O'Gorman's article reached him.
Papachristou does not cite O'Gorman 2005. Rhetorical-tradition phantasia scholarship outside Papachristou's analytic-Thomistic bibliography.
Papachristou does not cite González 2006. Papachristou treats De Anima phantasia, not Rhetoric III.1 phantasia; discipline split.
Papachristou does not cite Hawhee 2011. Rhetorical-vision scholarship outside Papachristou's bibliography.
